clue.text: Araucaria's day — important with a 9

parts.note: Mon is the short form of Monday
key means vital or important, as in a key witness
the 9 across entry, a grid of clues set for solving, stands for its generic name

explanation.surface: A tribute to the late setter Araucaria: a day made special by a puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: Araucaria was a beloved Guardian setter who took his pseudonym from the Latin name of the tree; 'with' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Araucaria is the botanical genus name of the spiky South American conifer known by this popular name.

clue.text: Far from pure setter perhaps outlining principles (we hear) in academic cruciverbalism, named Ximenes

indicators.note: the mongrel's letters draw a line around the initials, enclosing them

parts.note: a setter is a breed of dog, and one far from pure-bred is a mutt, a mongrel

indicators.note: principles sounds like principals, the leading letters, so take the first letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A description of a famously strict crossword setter who championed rigorous principles in academic puzzle-setting.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter is a dog, not a compiler. The sound-alike principles/principals is the signal for initial letters A, C, N.
explanation.definitionFit: Ximenes was the pseudonym of Derrick Somerset Macnutt, the Observer setter whose rules govern fair cryptic clueing.

clue.text: Biblical character, model from Somalia, eating nothing up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from the bottom, backwards
the model's name takes the zero inside it, as if swallowing it

parts.note: Iman is the Somali-born supermodel
O, the zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: A Somali model's name is turned up, like a famous fashion figure eating nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: Inserting O into IMAN gives IMOAN, which 'up' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Naomi is the mother-in-law of Ruth in the Old Testament Book of Ruth.

clue.text: Relaxed and informal — though hard on the way back?

definitions.meaning: a trip that is effortless heading out, perhaps downhill, must be tough on the return journey

explanation.surface: A laid-back person, perhaps a walker, whose route out was effortless but whose return trip is a slog.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes the phrase literally: if the outward going is easy, the coming back might be hard.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone tolerant and placid, not strict or fussy, is described by this hyphenated adjective.

clue.text: Some bread on better sort of desk

parts.note: a roll is a small loaf of bread
to top something is to better or beat it

explanation.surface: A baker's choice of loaf placed on a superior style of writing desk.
explanation.definitionFit: This kind of desk has a flexible slatted cover that slides down over the writing surface.

clue.text: Standard wine label

parts.note: red is a colour of wine, a glass of red
to flag is to mark or label something for attention

explanation.surface: An ordinary, regular label stuck on a bottle of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Standard' looks like an adjective describing the wine; it is a banner.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard is a banner, and this one is the emblem of socialism or a warning signal.

clue.text: Solver's Scottish isle

definitions.meaning: Colin Dexter named him after a champion cryptic solver
the northern part of the largest island of the Outer Hebrides

explanation.surface: A crossword solver's island home in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is'. Inspector Lewis is a British TV detective from the Inspector Morse series and its sequel.
explanation.definitionFit: A detective solves crimes, and the Hebridean isle shares the name of Oxford's fictional sergeant-turned-inspector.

clue.text: Reproof left man tired at first, during the course of life

indicators.note: the inner letters come during, that is within, the philosophical Way

parts.note: the Tao, in Chinese philosophy, is the Way, the path or course of life
the king is a man, a piece, in chess

indicators.note: take only the opening letter of the word tired

explanation.surface: A tired man is told off at some point in life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'during' places the man and his fellows within the Way; the Tao is the central idea of Taoist philosophy.
explanation.definitionFit: A reproof is a scolding, a dressing-down given to someone who has misbehaved.

clue.text: See 1 across
Shifty hooligan not entirely revolutionary

indicators.note: the word for a thug appears but lacks its final letter, so is not complete

parts.note: a lout is a yob or hooligan
Che Guevara, the Argentine revolutionary

explanation.surface: A shifty thug who is only partly a revolutionary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not entirely' drops the T of LOUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Louche means disreputable or of dubious character, in a rakish way, so shady or shifty.

clue.text: Our moment the mark of love — guarantee a number captivated by 100-year celebration finally coming around

parts.note: an X at the end of a letter marks a kiss, a sign of love
giving your word is a promise or guarantee

indicators.note: the number is held captive inside the rearranged letters

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100

indicators.note: these letters come round into a new order, a signal to rearrange them
take only the last letter of the word celebration

parts.note: ten is a number

explanation.surface: Celebrating love with a promise and a centenary party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming around' rearranges C, YEAR and N into CENARY, and 'captivated by' puts TEN inside it. The phrase is a made-up one for the 1913 to 2013 anniversary.
explanation.definitionFit: This puzzle marked a hundred years since the first such grid appeared, so this hundred-year anniversary is the solvers' own moment.

clue.text: Steps taken to back fringes in Zionist decree

indicators.note: the whole assembled run is taken back, so it reads in reverse
only the outermost letters of Zionist, its fringes, are used

parts.note: a law is a decree or statute

explanation.surface: Measures adopted to support the edges of a Zionist ruling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken to back' turns the whole assembled run round, not one piece alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballroom dance is a sequence of steps, and this one is in triple time.

clue.text: Neanderthal's comment about evildoing

indicators.note: the caveman's grunt goes about, or around, the wrong

parts.note: ug is the grunt cartoon cavemen are given
sin is wrongdoing or evil

explanation.surface: A caveman grunts his opinion about some wickedness.
explanation.walkthrough: A lift-and-separate clue: read 'evildoing' as 'evil doing', where evil gives SIN and doing is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something with a tool means employing it, so doing can stand for employing.

clue.text: Heavenly composition of Satie — little room to accommodate it

indicators.note: the small room holds or houses the rearranged letters

parts.note: a cell is a small room, as in a prison or monastery

indicators.note: a composition puts letters together in a new arrangement, playing on the composer

explanation.surface: A sublime piece by the composer Erik Satie, performed in a tiny room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composition of' rearranges SATIE into ESTIA, which 'to accommodate' puts inside CEL-L.
explanation.definitionFit: Celestial describes things of the sky or of heaven, so it is a synonym of heavenly.

clue.text: Dr Seuss's hat-wearer brought back hat — that's touching

indicators.note: the animal's name is brought back, read in reverse

parts.note: The Cat in the Hat is the Dr Seuss children's book
tile is old slang for a hat

explanation.surface: The Cat in the Hat gets his hat returned, which is touching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought back' turns CAT into TAC.
explanation.definitionFit: Tactile means relating to the sense of touch, perceptible by feel.

clue.text: See 9
Farm managed to divide farm produce the wrong way

indicators.note: the inner word splits the reversed produce in two
the produce is written the wrong way round

parts.note: eggs are produce from the farm
ran means managed, as in ran a business

explanation.surface: A farm was run so as to split its produce badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the wrong way' turns EGG into GGE, and RAN goes between its Gs.
explanation.definitionFit: A grange is a country house with farm buildings, or a farm itself.

clue.text: Extremes in a despot, remarkable

indicators.note: remarkable here means able to be marked anew, a signal to rework the letters

explanation.surface: Extreme behaviour seen in a remarkable tyrant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remarkable' rearranges IN A DESPOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Antipodes are places diametrically opposite on the globe, hence polar opposites or extremes.

clue.text: 7 good to keep in a dark hole? On the contrary

indicators.note: flips the clue's direction: the hole holds the good, and the whole is then written backwards
one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: a mine is a dark hole in the ground

explanation.surface: Is the 7 answer good to be stored in a dark pit? No, the opposite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the contrary' does double work: A MINE keeps G inside (AMGINE), not the reverse, and the result is reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: An enigma is a mystery or riddle, something baffling to be worked out.

clue.text: Difficult few days in trophy

indicators.note: the abbreviated span of days sits inside the trophy

parts.note: an award is a prize or trophy
WK, a week, is a few days

explanation.surface: Holding on to a trophy for only a few days is tricky.
explanation.definitionFit: Awkward means hard to deal with, clumsy, or troublesome.

clue.text: 9s, we could argue, in part for mankind

indicators.note: the letters are found lying within the words part for mankind

explanation.surface: A setter argues that his grids are, in part, an artistic contribution to humanity.
explanation.definitionFit: The setter is claiming that cryptic grids are a creative genre, a type of artistic expression.

clue.text: Right this day in New York initially, a new, extraordinary 9 inventor

indicators.note: the abbreviations sit within the rearranged letters
extraordinary marks the letters as rearranged into an unusual order
take the first letter of New and of York

parts.note: Thur, short for Thursday, the day the puzzle was published

explanation.surface: Celebrating the inventor of the grid on this very day in New York, a century on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extraordinary' rearranges N, Y, A, NEW into A WYNNE, and 'in' puts R THUR after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: This Liverpool-born journalist devised the first such word grid for the New York World in December 1913.

clue.text: Torquemada's hamster tortured

indicators.note: tortured means twisted out of shape, apt given the Spanish Inquisitor's name

explanation.surface: The Grand Inquisitor torments a pet rodent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tortured' rearranges HAMSTER. Torquemada was the pen name of the Observer's first cryptic setter.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Powys Mathers set fiendish Observer puzzles under the pseudonym of the Spanish Inquisitor.

clue.text: Take over something at the top of the flagpole, say?

indicators.note: say signals that the words are spoken, and spelling differs from sound

parts.words: something at the top of the flagpole
parts.note: a jack is a small flag, and one flying at the top of a pole is high

explanation.surface: A question about what flies at the masthead.
explanation.definitionFit: To seize control of a vehicle or a meeting by force is to commandeer it.

clue.text: Range of features I knitted together with one suspect?

indicators.note: suspect means doubtful or dodgy, a signal that the letters are not in their proper order

parts.note: the Roman numeral I stands for one

explanation.surface: Someone knits a set of faces together to match a suspect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'together with' just joins the pieces; 'suspect' rearranges I, KNITTED and I.
explanation.definitionFit: Police composite pictures were first built from a kit of interchangeable eyes, noses and mouths.

clue.text: Country's capital city its old capital has moved to

indicators.note: the final pair of letters of the old capital are shifted to the front, as the seat of government moved

parts.note: Kyoto was Japan's capital for over a thousand years

explanation.surface: A country's present capital is where its former capital was relocated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has moved' takes the TO of KYOTO to its front; the final 'to' doubles as a hint to those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Japan's present seat of government and largest metropolis.

clue.text: Flier — something to take with it

parts.note: take a pew means sit down, so a pew is something you take

explanation.surface: An invitation to bring something along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The lapwing, a crested plover, is a bird named for its call, so a flier.

clue.text: See 19
A jet won't start, I'm sad to say

indicators.note: the colour word is missing its first letter

parts.note: jet black is a deep shiny black

explanation.surface: Sad news: a jet engine fails to start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'won't start' drops the B of BLACK.
explanation.definitionFit: Alack is an archaic exclamation of regret or sorrow, like alas.

clue.text: Wealth in a Bath or Chelsea trip?

parts.note: Bath and Chelsea buns are British sweet bread rolls
to trip is to dance lightly, as in trip the light fantastic

explanation.surface: Is a smart trip to the posh town of Bath or Chelsea a sign of wealth?
explanation.walkthrough: Bath buns and Chelsea buns are traditional British sweet buns, named after an English city and a London district.
explanation.definitionFit: Plenty or a great quantity, of riches especially, means affluence.

clue.text: In New York World's case, 25's ultimate access to cipher

indicators.note: New signals a new arrangement of the letters that follow
the case of a word is its outer shell, the first and last letters
take the final letter of the name at 25 down

explanation.surface: Wynne's first grid ran in the New York World newspaper, here pictured as a code-breaking key.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges YORK, WD (the case of WORLD) and E (the last letter of WYNNE). The paper ran Wynne's first grid in December 1913.
explanation.definitionFit: A code word used to encrypt and decrypt a message unlocks the coded text.

clue.text: Judge the character of Jenny?

definitions.meaning: to judge is to evaluate or appraise
a jenny is a female donkey, so in character she is a she-ass, playfully a female ass with the -ess suffix

explanation.surface: Evaluate what kind of person Jenny really is.
explanation.walkthrough: A jenny is a female donkey; adding the feminine ending -ESS to ASS gives a jokey word for her.
explanation.definitionFit: To evaluate or appraise something's worth or quality is to weigh it up.
